advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a gitleaks regression test (mirroring test_repo_gitleaks_config_allowlists_doc_throwaway_but_not_real_secret) asserting the fake single-'x'-body PEM shape is allowlisted by the committed .gitleaks.toml while a real long-random-body PEM key in the same scan is still flagged.
evidence: Added allowlist regex: '-----BEGIN[ A-Z]*PRIVATE KEY-----(?:\\\\n|\\n|\n)x(?:\\\\n|\\n|\n)-----END[ A-Z]*PRIVATE KEY-----' (.gitleaks.toml:63-65)

Existing harness that the change did not extend: tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py:378 test_repo_gitleaks_config_allowlists_doc_throwaway_but_not_real_secret — runs gitleaks with/without the committed .gitleaks.toml and asserts the throwaway is allowlisted while a genuine secret still trips
search of tests/ for 'PRIVATE KEY' / 'BEGIN DSA' finds no test asserting the new PEM allowlist behavior (the fake-PEM ids are suppressed AND a real long-body key still trips)

Named violating inputs covered by the added regex: fake id '-----BEGIN DSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nx\n-----END DSA PRIVATE KEY-----' (expected suppressed) vs. a header + long random body + END line (expected still flagged)
advisory.finding: The newly added .gitleaks.toml allowlist for the fake-PEM test-id shape has no regression test, although the repo has an established harness for exactly this (test_repo_gitleaks_config_allowlists_doc_throwaway_but_not_real_secret). The commit's behavioral claim — the fake PEM shape is suppressed (3→0 findings) while a real long-body key is still flagged — is unverified by any committed test, so a later regex loosening that also hides genuine PEM leaks would go undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CI/pre-commit check (or documented refresh cadence) that fails when .test_durations keys diverge from the current default test selection.
evidence: Commit message: 'The profile holds 19,862 keys for the 19,862 tests of the default selection'
No CI/pre-commit hook in the diff checks that .test_durations keys match the current test selection
advisory.finding: The committed .test_durations is a machine-generated artifact (~2.6 MB, 19,862 keys) with no checked-in provenance pin tying it to a specific pytest-split version or test-suite revision; it can silently go stale as tests are added/removed, and nothing in the diff enforces regeneration.
scenarios: A new test file is added but .test_durations is not refreshed, so pytest-split silently mis-balances groups with no gate catching the drift

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain the fake-PEM gitleaks allowlist with a `paths` entry limited to `^\.test_durations$` so the exemption cannot apply to other tracked files.
evidence: Comment: 'Scoped to that exact fake shape, never a path/test exclusion.' — scoped by shape, applies repo-wide
The allowlist has no `paths` constraint limiting it to .test_durations
advisory.finding: The new gitleaks allowlist regex for fake PEM shapes broadens the global secret-scan allowlist by match-content rather than by path, so any future file (not just .test_durations) containing a one-char-body PEM will be silently exempted from leak detection.
scenarios: A genuinely short placeholder/test key with a single-char body is committed outside the test-id context and is not flagged because the allowlist is content-scoped, not path-scoped
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `paths = ['''^\.test_durations$''']` constraint to the new `[[allowlists]]` block so the match-content exemption only applies within the generated profile.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider a bounded guard (e.g. a dedicated hook with a higher explicit cap) for .test_durations instead of a blanket exclusion so unbounded growth is still caught.
evidence: Commit message: 'exempt it from the 500 KB check-added-large-files cap (2.6 MB)'
Exemption fully excludes the file from the hook; no per-file upper bound remains
advisory.finding: The check-added-large-files exemption is widened to a regex alternation that also matches on untracked siblings (e.g. the pattern `^(uv\.lock|\.test_durations)$` is anchored, which is fine) but the 2.6 MB profile is now permanently exempted with no size ceiling, so unbounded future growth of .test_durations bypasses the 500 KB cap entirely.
scenarios: The suite grows to hundreds of thousands of tests and .test_durations balloons to tens of MB, bloating clone/fetch sizes with no gate flagging it
